During the Federal war in the United States a new and influential club was established in the city of Baltimore in the State of Maryland.
It is well known with what energy the taste for military inventions was then developed among the brotherhood of artillerists.
During the duration of the war they were never weary of inventing guns of extraordinary dimensions, and in that respect they left far behind them the famous bombards of the Middle Ages.
All these inventors, men of great merit and of undoubted genius, only thought of one thing—how to invent engines of war capable of carrying projectiles of many thousand pounds to a great distance.
